standard.title: Rules and laws
standard.description: the differences between 'rules' and 'laws', why laws are important and how they affect the lives of people
standard.strand: Knowledge and Understanding — Civics and Citizenship
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y3 (AC9HS3K06): Students explored who makes rules, why rules are important and the consequences of not following them.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students distinguish between rules and laws, explain why laws are important and describe how they affect people's lives.

nodes.label: Distinguishing rules from laws
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can distinguish between rules (contextual, limited scope) and laws (universal, enforceable) and give examples of each.
nodes.minimum_width: Give at least two examples of rules and two of laws and explain the key difference between them.
nodes.typical_width: Distinguish between laws (not speeding in school zones) and rules (sun safety at school); explore examples of laws and their purposes; recognise that laws apply to everyone in society.
wider: Investigate how a rule at school compares with a similar law in the community and discuss what makes the difference in scope and enforcement
Explore First Nations Australian customary lore and discuss how it functions like law within communities
nodes.hinge_reason: The rule/law distinction is the conceptual foundation of civics understanding at Year 4 — without it, students cannot analyse how laws affect people's lives in Node 2.

response_modes.reason: Rule vs law is a conceptual distinction requiring explicit criteria — use a comparison matrix with scope, maker, enforcer and applicability columns.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations Australian customary lore provides a third model of collective behaviour regulation (alongside rules and laws) that enriches the civic concept significantly.
success_criteria: Gives at least two examples each of rules and laws
Explains at least one key difference between rules and laws

nodes.label: How laws affect people's lives
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how specific laws affect the lives of people, including the impact of environmental and native title laws on First Nations Australians.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe how at least one law affects the daily life of people.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate the impact of laws on students' lives; explore how environmental laws, native title laws and laws concerning sacred sites affect specific groups including First Nations Australians.
wider: Investigate native title law in depth and explain how it was established and what it means for First Nations Australian communities
Research the customary lore of a specific First Nations Australian group and discuss how it governs community life

response_modes.reason: Laws affecting different groups (general community vs First Nations Australians vs environmental users) reveal that laws have differential impacts.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Native title and sacred site laws directly connect civics to First Nations Australian history and create a concrete example of how laws can both affect and protect specific groups.
success_criteria: Describes how at least one specific law affects people's lives
Identifies that laws can affect different groups differently
